I love how it offers not only knowledge tests, but prep for endorsements too! I also love the multiple-choice simulation and how an explanation is provided for the correct answer-choice. One suggestion to improve the app would be to incorporate live, realistic videos that demonstrate the entire pre-trip inspection, simulation of the skills and road test, and the different parts of the tractor and trailer components (I.e., air brake system, engine compartment, etc.), because reading alone is not enough to comprehend and remember all those complex systems. I believe that hands-on practice is the best way to remember most of this material. text:
I have been using this app for about a week. I will be taking my CDL permit written test tomorrow, and will update with the results and how they compare to this prep app. I will say that I do like how this app is structured for the most part. However I am disappointed that there is no way for the test thing to synchronize across multiple devices. For example I have this app on both my iPhone and my iPad and it would be nice for my progress to update across both devices as are use which ever is most convenient for me at any given moment. The fact that they do not synchronize means my phone on my iPad do not know the progress of my prep work on the other, which is extremely annoying.

UPDATE: So I used this app to study for my CDL, B, P Air Brakes permit for Michigan. I passed all 3 tests on the first try. And I scored 100% on the Brakes and Passenger endorsement tests. I’ll agree that MOST of the practice questions (I’ll call it 95+%) were EXACTLY the questions on the test at the SOS office. There was a small number of questions on my actual General Knowledge test that I was seeing for the first time while testing. (I got 6 wrong out of the allowable 10, and the test still ended automatically once I had 40 correct of 50). So, was it worth $15?  To me, yes. Absolutely. It is VERY MUCH “teaching the test” as an approach, which, philosophically, may not be ideal for actually learning all the concepts and such. But that’s what the state manual is for. I took ALL the practice tests, answering all the challenge bank questions between them.  I did this until I passed them all. I took all of the mock exams, passed them all. I spent about a week on this. I still would like to see SYNC options across devices, but I’m pleased with my purchase. It was worth it to me!!

title: Felt Familiar on Test Day
text:
I started using this app to study for my CDL permit for a few weeks ago and took my permit test last week. 
What stood out to me was how familiar the questions felt once the exam started. A lot of them weren’t long or detailed — they were short and easy to misread if you didn’t slow down. That felt very similar to how I’d been practicing.
There were a few moments where I caught myself almost rushing, then stopped and reread the question, because that’s what I’d gotten used to doing in the app.
I passed the test, and it didn’t feel like luck. It felt like I’d trained for the way the questions are actually written.
Everyone studies differently, but for me, this app matched the real exam more closely than I expected.

title: Air Brakes Section Actually Helps
text:

The flashcards helped too. Air brakes got a lot of small stuff that gets mixed up, and seeing it a few times made it stick better than just reading the manual.
